scenes.headline: How a 20B model packs into 5.31 GB
scenes.sub: Maple-Preview: weights trained to be minus one, zero or plus one.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lilac! Maple-Preview is a twenty billion parameter reasoning model where nearly every weight is minus one, zero or plus one.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Don't quantize after training. Train the weights to be ternary: three values per row.
scenes.mark: Train the weights to be ternary
scenes.say: Most quantization happens after training. Maple's weights were trained ternary: each row holds three values, with its own scale.

scenes.title: One weight row, read from the bytes

steps.label: bf16: about two thousand distinct values
steps.say: A normal bf16 weight row of two thousand forty-eight numbers has around two thousand distinct values.

steps.label: ternary: minus s, zero, plus s
steps.note: 38-43% of each row is exactly zero
steps.say: Read a row of Maple's published bytes and there are exactly three. Thirty-eight to forty-three percent are exactly zero, and s changes row to row.
Twenty-four layers, each with attention and two hundred fifty-six experts. A token visits eight; there's no shared expert.

steps.note: a 512-token window on three of every four layers
steps.say: Three of every four layers only see a five hundred twelve token window, so a long context still fits on a Mac mini.
The router stays full precision, since three levels would scramble which expert fires. So do the embeddings. Everything else is ternary.

scenes.title: Why 5.31 GB
scenes.say: Each ternary weight carries about one point five eight five bits. The checkpoint works out to one point six five.

parts.say: Five ternary weights have two hundred forty-three combinations.

parts.note: one byte, plus a scale per row
parts.say: A byte holds two hundred fifty-six, so five weights fit in a byte. That's about where one point six five lands.

scenes.label: what the Hugging Face repository ships: ternary values stored unpacked, as bf16
scenes.note: the packed checkpoint and ternary kernels are unreleased
scenes.say: One catch: the repository ships forty point four three gigabytes, the ternary values stored unpacked. The packed file and its kernels aren't released.

scenes.text: Train ternary from the start and a 20B model lands near the entropy floor. Then the vocabulary is what's left to shrink.
scenes.say: So train ternary from the start, and the model lands near the entropy floor. What's left to shrink is the vocabulary.

recap: Weights trained ternary, one scale per row
Routers and embeddings stay full precision
scenes.say: To recap: trained ternary, sharp routers, and five weights to a byte.
